summary: Rerank returns inconsistent top-k order and occasional NaN scores after model fallback; latency spike observed
description:
Issue summary:
LogiSearch (dedicated) reports that their /rerank endpoint started returning inconsistent top-k ordering for identical requests after a backend capacity event. In several requests the top scores are valid but the downstream returned ordering changes between retries; in ~7% of sampled calls we see NaN similarity scores and in others we see many ties (same score) that previously were distinct.

Impact:
- Customer-facing search quality regression: users see inconsistent ordering for the same query.
- Intermittent NaN scores cause downstream dedup/thresholding code to drop results.
- Latency for rerank calls spiked from typical 200-400ms to 2-5s during the incident window.
- Affects production traffic in us-east; approximate affected sessions ~0.6% of requests in last 12h.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment for LogiSearch in us-east region.
- Primary embeddings model: redwood-open-embed-1.3q (GPU).
- Fallback reranker variant observed: rdrk-rerank-v2-cpu-quant (CPU quantized).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Send rerank request with payload: top_candidates=500, queries=single short text, embeddings requested with model redwood-open-embed-1.3q.
2) Force a capacity event by draining a pool (customer reproduced during a scheduled maintenance window).
3) Observe rerank response ordering change across 3 quick retries and occasional NaN in the scores array.

Observed logs (snippets):
- "2026-03-10T09:32:14Z ERR reranker: score computation resulted in NaN for candidate_id=3742 (module: dot_product)"
- "2026-03-10T09:32:14Z WARN serving-runtime: falling back to rdrk-rerank-v2-cpu-quant due to no GPU slot"
- "2026-03-10T09:32:15Z INFO api-gateway: request_id=abc123 latency=3421ms route=/rerank"

Additional notes about payload shapes:
- Customer payload embeddings are 1024-d by contract. The GPU model produces 1024-d float32 vectors. The CPU quantized reranker expects 1024-d int8-symmetric packed tensors after dequantization path, but our fallback path performs a normalization step that may assume float inputs.

Requested outcome:
- Root cause analysis and fix to prevent NaN/tie scores when fallback occurs, or a recommended customer-side mitigation until fix is live.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer dedicated stack in us-east with same API key and send a rerank request with top_candidates=500. 2) Simulate capacity event (drain pool) so requests route to fallback model. 3) Retry same payload 3-5 times and compare top-k ordering and score arrays. 4) Inspect logs for NaN and fallback warnings.

investigation_notes: 03/10 10:00 - Support triage: confirmed customer reproduces issue when fallback to CPU quantized reranker occurs.
03/10 12:30 - SRE captured CPU-side logs: several dot_product ops return NaN immediately after dequant path for inputs with all zeros in one candidate (edge case).

03/11 09:15 - Eng hypothesis: normalization order mismatch — quantized path may be applying quantize->dot->normalize vs expected normalize->dot in GPU path, producing numerical instability for near-zero vectors.

03/11 15:40 - Reproduced locally by forcing reranker to use rdrk-rerank-v2-cpu-quant on a short synthetic query set; saw same NaNs when candidate vectors contain zero-padding after tokenization/embedding mismatch.
03/12 08:20 - Identified a missing float-clamp step in the CPU dequant routine that allows tiny denormals to propagate and produce NaNs in the dot product in rare cases.
Next steps: patch dequant clamp and add explicit L2-normalize-before-dot for CPU reranker; run canary for LogiSearch pool.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:02 - Joanna (Support): Received report from LogiSearch CS. Assigned to ENG for deeper triage.
2026-03-10 13:05 - Ethan Cole (Eng): I can reproduce locally when forcing fallback. Dumped raw dequant tensors; several entries are all zeros after unpacking — suspect packing/unpacking mismatch.
2026-03-11 10:00 - Priya Shah (Support): Customer confirmed issue started right after an autoscaler event at ~09:30 UTC; provided request_id=abc123 for trace.
2026-03-11 16:00 - SRE (Alex Ramos): Placed temporary policy to prefer GPU pool unless latency > 3s; reduces customer exposure while we work on fix.
workaround: Temporary mitigation: 1) Customer can pin reranker to a non-quantized variant (rdrk-rerank-v2) via the model pinning API to avoid fallback path until fix is deployed. 2) We deployed a serving policy change to prefer GPU pools for LogiSearch (will increase cost but reduce errors).
resolution_notes: Patch for dequant clamp and explicit L2-normalize-before-dot prepared (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/reranker/pull/7456). Will run unit tests for edge-case zeros and a canary rollout to LogiSearch pool in us-east. Targeting full rollout after validation on 2026-03-13.
estimated_impact: ~0.6% of rerank traffic for LogiSearch in last 12h; customer reported user-facing ordering inconsistencies and some dropped results due to NaNs.
next_steps: Merge dequant clamp PR after review
Run canary in us-east for LogiSearch dedicated pool
Monitor token-level and rerank-score histograms for NaN/inf occurrences
Postmortem draft if canary shows reduction to <0.01% NaN rate
